ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (33) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

Tolstoy's retelling of Hugo's poem keeps its shifts between present and past tense and the Russian dialogue dashes, as in the January “Thief's Son”; «полог» (polog, 'bed curtain') is “curtain” each time, and the dead widow keeps the name Tolstoy gives her, «Симон» (Simon). The husband's «Прибьет он меня!» (Prib'yot on menya, 'he'll beat me') is not raised to “kill.”

Source observation: [26] Stray Markdown asterisks «** » after «как сердце болело!» (between two sentences) look like a transcription artefact (empty bold or lost footnote mark); omitted in the English.
